title: Eligible is not the same as suitable
objectives: Spot the red flags for each check.
Explain why PMS sits on top of a core portfolio.
body_md:
Meeting the ₹50 lakh minimum makes a client eligible, not suitable. PMS should sit on top of a solid core portfolio, never replace it.

## Suitability checklist

| Question | Suitable if… | Red flag |
|---|---|---|
| Investible surplus | ₹50 lakh is a slice of a larger portfolio | It is most of the client's investible wealth |
| Existing core | Already has diversified MFs, debt and emergency funds | No core portfolio; PMS would be the first equity |
| Horizon | 3–5+ years without needing the money | May need it within 2–3 years |
| Drawdown tolerance | Has stayed invested through a 30%+ fall before | Has never seen a real market fall, or sold in one |
| Tax awareness | Understands each trade creates a tax event | Expects MF-like tax deferral |
| Engagement | Comfortable with monthly statements and a full trade list | Wants something hands-off and simple |
example: A business owner has exactly ₹55 lakh in total savings and wants ₹50 lakh in PMS. That is nearly all of his wealth with no core portfolio, which is a red flag. Suggest mutual funds first, or PMS only as a slice later.
say: PMS should be a part of your portfolio, not all of it. How would you feel if this portion fell 30% in a year?
Meeting the ₹50 lakh minimum makes you eligible, not suitable.
never: You have the ₹50 lakh, so PMS is right for you.

check.q: A client has exactly ₹55 lakh in total savings and wants ₹50 lakh in PMS. What is correct?
o: Suitable, because the ₹50 lakh minimum is met
Suitable if the strategy has strong past returns
Invest the full ₹55 lakh to qualify for lower fees
Eligible but not suitable; suggest MFs first, PMS later
check.why: Eligible is not suitable. That is 91% of their savings, with no core portfolio and no emergency buffer.

check.q: Which client profile is a red flag for PMS?
o: PMS would be the client's first equity investment
Client has a diversified MF and debt core
Client stayed invested through a 30% fall
check.why: PMS should sit on top of a solid core portfolio, never replace it.

check.q: What is the minimum horizon for a suitable PMS client?
check.why: If the client may need the money within 2–3 years, it is a red flag.
